task_name: `Header.tsx` y `StaleNotice.tsx`: la frescura de la foto

rubric.result:
The objective promises four things and all four are in the diff. (1) The header reads the vocabularies instead of the field pair: HeaderProps drops `meta` and takes `history: HeaderHistory` / `snapshot: SnapshotNotice`, and the three derived consts (`lastCommitAt`/`fetchedAt`/`stale`) are gone (Header.tsx). (2) It says there is no history when there is none: `case 'none': return
{NO_HISTORY_META}
` (Header.tsx:107-108), with NO_HISTORY_META = 'sin historial · ningún commit todavía' from format.ts:175. (3) A clone fetched more than seven days ago shows its banner: App.tsx:95 `{snapshot.kind === 'stale' && }` plus the new StaleNotice.tsx, and the stale header line in Header.tsx:135-138. (4) A clone that never fetched shows neither date nor banner: `case 'never-fetched': return null` (Header.tsx:129-130) and the banner condition is false for that member. The threshold itself is not re-derived anywhere: staleness comes from `clone.stale` via ScreenChoice.snapshotOf.

The TDD line names `test('a clone that never fetched shows neither a fetch date nor the banner')` and fixes the assertion: with `fetchedAt: null` there is neither `traída` nor `Foto local desactualizada`, and the clone path on screen proves the load arrived. The test in the diff asserts exactly that, in that order: `await screen.findByText('/git/alpha')`, then `queryByText(/traída/)).toBeNull()`, then `queryByText(/Foto local desactualizada/)).toBeNull()`. The `fetchedAt: null` is set on the Clone (`CloneMother.neverFetched()`), which is the right subject per the closed decision 'De dónde sale la frescura de la foto | Del Clone que devuelve GET /repos, nunca de summary.meta'; the double is additionally made hostile by leaving `meta.fetchedAt` populated, so a header still reading `meta` would fail the second assertion. Same assertion, same input, same expected value as the written phrase.

Both Contract blocks match name by name. HeaderProps in the diff declares `repos: readonly Clone[]`, `repoId: string`, `onRepo: (id: string) => void`, `window: TimeWindow`, `onWindow: (window: TimeWindow) => void`, `history: HeaderHistory`, `snapshot: SnapshotNotice`, `now: Date` — same names, same types, same order as the brief, and `meta` is gone as the brief requires. The `Current state` block (the three derived consts at Header.tsx:24-26) is removed. StaleNotice.tsx declares `export interface BannerProps { fetchedAt: string; now: Date }` and `export class StaleNotice { static Banner(...): ReactElement }`; `fetchedAt` is a bare `string`, which is what the vocabulary members `fresh`/`stale` guarantee. `HeaderHistory`/`SnapshotNotice` are imported from `./screen`, where task 1 declared them, and `ScreenChoice.of` already returns `{ screen, history, snapshot }`, which App.tsx now destructures whole. The Spanish copy consumed (`NO_HISTORY_META`, `freshSnapshotLine`, `staleSnapshotLine`, `staleBannerSentence`) exists in format.ts with the literal text the plan fixed.

Row by row on the rows this diff bears on: freshness from the Clone and never from summary.meta — implemented (Header no longer receives `meta`; `snapshot` comes from ScreenChoice.snapshotOf, which reads `clone.fetchedAt`/`clone.stale`); the server decides staleness and the interface does not repeat the seven-day threshold — implemented (no arithmetic on the threshold anywhere in the diff); new Spanish lives in format.ts — implemented (every new string is a format.ts export; the pre-existing `último commit` literal stays inline because the brief says `last-commit` keeps today's text); a new .tsx module exposes its components as static methods of a class named for the concept — implemented (`class StaleNotice { static Banner }`); a module that was already there keeps its default export — implemented (`export default function Header`); one `load: SummaryLoad` — untouched and preserved. The single deviation is the row 'Cómo se despacha en TSX sin rama por defecto': it fixes the declared return type at `ReactElement`, and the two new dispatch functions declare `ReactElement | null`. Reported as low, because the row's load-bearing effect survives (with `strict: true` in tsconfig.base.json, a switch exhaustive over the union makes the end of the function unreachable; a new member makes it reachable and TS2366 fires, since `undefined` is not in `ReactElement | null`) and because the task text itself requires two members to draw nothing.

conventions/defects.md, rule by rule. (1) Closed vocabulary: this is the diff's whole subject and it is on the right side of the rule — the header stops deriving state from `meta?.stale === true` / `meta?.fetchedAt ?? null` and dispatches over `HeaderHistory` and `SnapshotNotice`, with no catch-all in either switch (Header.tsx:104-116 and 128-139) and the absent states (`unknown`, `never-fetched`) declared as members rather than optionals. Noted, not counted: App.tsx:95 asks `snapshot.kind === 'stale'` outside the dispatch, which is a second place touching that partition (conventions/decisions.md: 'The same partition of a closed vocabulary declared in more than one place'); it is prescribed verbatim by the task ('App.tsx dibuja <StaleNotice.Banner …/> … solo cuando snapshot.kind === "stale"'), it answers a different question (whether the banner renders, not which line the header draws), and the classification of a clone as stale still lives once in screen.ts. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: no subject — nothing in the diff returns or consumes a map; props are declared interfaces and `CloneMother` returns the `Clone` contract type. (3) Two fields that have to agree, including sentinels: this diff removes one — the `fetchedAt`/`stale` pair — and introduces none: `SnapshotNotice` carries the date only in the members that have one, and `BannerProps.fetchedAt` is non-nullable, so no empty string or epoch stands for 'never fetched'. (4) An error named for where it happens: no subject, the diff adds no error type. style.md: StaleNotice.tsx is a new module and is born conforming — no prose, English identifiers, everything hanging off the `StaleNotice` type including the two private style constants. Header.tsx and App.test.tsx are pre-existing hosts with doc comments and module-level functions, so the added `historyLine`/`snapshotLine`/`snapshotLineStyle` and their comments follow the host style under that document's declared debt, and they extend the header rather than introducing a new concept (the brief places them there). architecture.md (new modules): StaleNotice.tsx is one concept plus the props type that has no life without it, imports only its copy from format.ts, and crosses no boundary — web/ still imports nothing from server/ (AGENTS.md 'Frontera web/ ↔ server/'). AGENTS.md 'Code style & conventions': identifiers, comments and test names in English, visible copy in Spanish — respected; 'Security & data handling': no author name or email reaches the DOM. testing.md: the new tests assert the observable effect (literal DOM sentences), the objects come from a mother with named scenarios, and the doubles are the two endpoints the shell calls. Exemplars: App.test.tsx's fetch double is reused rather than re-invented, and Screens.tsx is the pattern StaleNotice.tsx follows (class, static component, private CSSProperties constants). Two plan-level gaps seen and not counted, neither reachable from this task's Files line: `@keyframes rp-sweep` exists in no file under web/src (only the reference at Screens.tsx:112), so the loading bar is static; and `meta.fetchedAt`/`meta.stale` are now read by no production line in web/src, but api/types.ts is outside this task.

The `-` lines in App.test.tsx are the `CLONES` literal turned into `CloneMother.fresh()` (fixture data, plus the comment moved onto the mother's method) and one arrange line: `-  stubApi({ lastCommitAt: null, fetchedAt: null, stale: false })` becomes `stubApi({ lastCommitAt: null, fetchedAt: null, stale: false }, {}, [CloneMother.neverFetched()])` in 'without dates the header shows neither'. No assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten: that test keeps all five of its expectations verbatim, and the arrange change is exactly what the objective and the closed decision demand (freshness now comes from the Clone, so the absence has to be stated on the clone or the test would stop being about an absence). No weakened assertion is left unaccounted for.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. The banner sentence asserted through `findByRole('status')` can only come from StaleNotice.tsx's `<div role="status">` plus the App.tsx:95 conditional; the header's stale and fresh lines come from Header.tsx's `snapshotLine` branches calling format.ts; `sin historial · ningún commit todavía` comes from the `case 'none'` branch reading the `NO_HISTORY_META` export. The doubles only supply the payload: each new test deliberately gives `summary.meta` the opposite freshness or a live last-commit date, so an implementation still reading `meta` — the code this diff deletes — would fail the assertions rather than pass them. Revert Header.tsx and StaleNotice.tsx and all four new tests fail.

Everything written inside the four declared files answers a sentence of the task. Header.tsx: the props swap, the two dispatch helpers and their style constants are the task's text. StaleNotice.tsx: the banner with the isStale styling and, as `### Out of scope` demands, no `Traer cambios` button — the new test even asserts `queryByRole('button', { name: 'Traer cambios' })).toBeNull()`. App.tsx: destructuring `history`/`snapshot`, the StaleNotice import and the one conditional render, nothing else (the `screenBody` dispatch and `codeOf` are untouched). App.test.tsx: the four tests the `**Tests:**` line names, plus `CloneMother` and the third `stubApi` parameter, which the new cases need in order to give three clones three freshness states and which conventions/testing.md asks for ('The objects a test needs are built by a mother'). No refactor, rename or adjacent fix beyond that; nothing named in `### Out of scope` appears.

The four new tests in App.test.tsx measured on the three blocking properties. Deterministic: they take the shell's real clock (App reads `new Date()` once and there is no seam for it in this task), and the assertions are written to be total over what that clock can produce — the fresh case accepts `(hoy|hace 1 día|hace \d+ días)`, the stale case pins the whole sentence and leaves only `\d+` to the day count over a date already six weeks past, so no forward run can flip them; no network, no filesystem, no randomness, no sleep. Isolated: each test builds its own `fetch` stub, which `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in the setup file undoes, the mother returns a fresh object per call, and no test depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on DOM text produced by the production code (the banner sentence, the two header lines, the no-history line) and none on a mock's call count or a constant the test defined; reverting Header.tsx/StaleNotice.tsx/App.tsx turns all four red. On the finer half I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and found nothing to pin: the two names carrying an 'and'/'neither…nor' ('a fresh clone shows its fetch date and no banner', 'a clone that never fetched shows neither a fetch date nor the banner') are the names the plan's `**Tests:**` line prescribes verbatim, so the wording is not the implementer's choice, and each still covers a single behaviour with its two halves being the presence and the absence of the same line.

findings.what: The closed decision fixes the declared return type of a TSX dispatch at `ReactElement`; the two new dispatch functions declare `ReactElement | null` instead. The row's load-bearing effect does survive — with `strict: true` (tsconfig.base.json) an exhaustive switch makes the end of the function unreachable, so adding a member to `HeaderHistory` or `SnapshotNotice` makes it reachable and TS2366 fires, because `undefined` is not part of `ReactElement | null` — and the task text itself requires two members ('unknown no pinta nada', 'never-fetched no pinta nada') to draw nothing, which the bare type only admits via an empty fragment. Low, not medium: the deviation is from the row's literal value, not from its purpose, and the alternative it forbids reads worse. Same deviation at Header.tsx:127 (`snapshotLine`).
findings.evidence: Brief §2: "Cómo se despacha en TSX sin rama por defecto | La función de despacho declara su tipo de retorno `ReactElement`, así que un miembro nuevo rompe la compilación" — diff: "function historyLine(history: HeaderHistory, now: Date): ReactElement | null {"
